Subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Lumos Health

Thanks again for taking the time today - quick recap from our discovery call and suggested next steps so we're all aligned. High level takeaways: 

Pain points
- Production latency spikes on peak scheduling windows (p95 generation time > 2.5s)
- Cost unpredictability with current cloud GPU burst model
- Regulatory requirement for data isolation for PHI handling in parts of the workload

Goals
- Stable p95 latency under 1.2s for core clinical-generation queries
- Isolated dedicated capacity (tenant isolation + VPC) to meet compliance
- Predictable monthly spend for budgeting and approvals

Recommended Redwood Dedicated configuration (initial proposal)
- Reserved pool: 6x A100-equivalent GPU GPUs (can scale to 8x during onboarding)
- Private deployment: VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for key rotation
- Autoscaling policy: vertical burst to 2x baseline for 10-minute windows; proactive warm pools for scheduled peaks
- SLA target: 99.95% uptime available for Dedicated customers with SLA add-on; target p95 token latency SLO 1.2s on typical request mix
- Operational: token-level cost dashboards, per-route tracing, and canary rollout for model updates

Open questions we flagged that I've put below as action items:
1) Confirmation on required GPU family (A100 vs H100) and any preferred instance SKUs from your infra team
2) Any specific egress / data residency constraints beyond US/region-level isolation
3) Procurement timeline and point of contact for statement-of-work / PO

Attachments: lumos_dedicated_sow_v1.pdf (SOW draft), lumos_capacity_matrix.xlsx (initial sizing + cost math)

Proposed next steps
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Rishi and your infra/security lead (I can set this up for next week)
- Share SOW and capacity matrix with procurement/legal; I'll follow up with a draft DocuSign link once we confirm scope
- If the sizing looks good, we'll do a two-week pilot with reduced commit to validate latency & isolation workflow

If that matches your notes, reply with confirmation on GPU preference and a couple windows that work for the deep dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Jamie / team - quick technical notes to address the H100 preference and KMS question.

- H100 support: Redwood Dedicated supports both A100 and H100-class hardware. For the model + quantization profile you described, H100 will give better throughput and lower tail latencies. We should size based on expected concurrency and sequence-length distribution; the attached capacity matrix includes an H100 column with throughput estimates.
- KMS integration: we support cross-account AWS KMS and customer-managed keys for both in-flight TLS and at-rest encryption of cached KV and traces. We'll send a short integration checklist for your infra team (service role, key policy snippet, and audit log hooks).
- Isolation & compliance: Dedicated provides tenant-level isolation, VPC peering, and optional on-prem box for fully air-gapped datasets if required. For PHI processing we recommend the private deployment + restricted ingress CIDR and long-term audit log retention (90+ days) - we can adjust retention to meet specific audit windows.
- SLA / uptime: with the SLA add-on we offer 99.95% monthly uptime for the Dedicated control plane and serving endpoints; SLOs for latency are measured per-model and per-route - we'll include p50/p95/p99 baselines in the pilot run report.
- Pilot & rollout: typical pilot cadence = 2 weeks (baseline test + load validation) followed by canary rollout across live routes for 1-2 weeks. Full prod commit commonly takes 3-6 weeks depending on procurement.

Next steps from engineering side:
- I'll send the KMS checklist and capacity_matrix H100 column by EOD.
- Propose a technical deep dive Tuesday/Wednesday next week - slots I have: Tue 10-12 PDT, Wed 14-16 PDT.

Happy to answer any specific infra/security questions before the call.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
